subject: `use lib "$ENV{HOME}/x"` — a double-quoted `use` argument is not interpolated
description:
DONE s374 (cbf6d71). SCOPE ANSWERED (the task asked): only TWO hand-rolled sites wrapped a token's RAW text in CL quotes — _process_use_lib and _compile_constant_value. A general `use Module LIST` already compiles its import args through _parse_expression.

Each was broken four ways at once, not just interpolation (probed):
  use lib "$ENV{HOME}/x"  -> the literal chars on @INC (surfacing later as "Can't locate X.pm in @INC" with the un-interpolated path — how it was found)
  use constant X => "a\nb" -> CL reads \n as n  -> "anb"  (silent wrong)
  use constant X => 'a\b'  -> CL eats the \     -> "ab"   (silent wrong)
  use constant X => 'a"b'  -> emits "a"b" — UNREADABLE CL, whole file dies at load

Both now use the ordinary expression path; the single-quote-token short-circuit in _compile_constant_value is DELETED (its own comment already said why NUMBERS must not be short-circuited — strings were the same trap one type over).

corpus-diff identical; the five constant-using lib/ shims byte-identical. Cache generation bumped to v2-125. Guard: five rows in Pl/t/use-require-01.t.
